.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Aviation section updated. Otherwise, no significant changes 
made to the forecast since the last update.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Mainly dry with above normal high temperatures. No significant 
weather impacts.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
A highly amplified flow across the Lower 48 will feature a 
building upper ridge over the mid section of the country 
expanding east through the week. This will result in a prolonged 
period of dry weather and above normal temperatures through at least 
Saturday if not the entire weekend. A cold front passing through 
Sunday night into Monday may have enough moisture to work with for a 
few showers, but impactful conditions are not expected.

After highs slightly above normal on Tuesday, high temps Wednesday 
through Sunday are expected to be 60-65 across the forecast area. 
Low temperature moderation will be bit a more gradual due to the dry 
airmass in place and decent radiational cooling.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
High pressure remains near the region through the TAF period, 
centered just west of the region. Dry and VFR conditions are 
expected to prevail through the TAF period. 

Wind speeds will be mostly 5 kts tonight into Tuesday morning, and 
closer to 10 kt for the late Tuesday morning and Tuesday afternoon 
period. The wind direction will be generally from the WNW-NW tonight 
into early Tuesday and then generally out of the WSW-WNW for Tuesday 
afternoon into early Tuesday evening. Wind speeds near 5-10 kts 
expected Tuesday night.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Wind directions could be off by 20-30 degrees from TAF at 
times Tuesday afternoon.

.OUTLOOK FOR 06Z Wednesday through Saturday... 

Late Tonight-Saturday: VFR.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
High pressure will remain in control of the weather through the week 
with sub-SCA conditions. Winds will mostly  be from the NW-W at less 
than 15kt with seas on the ocean no higher than 2 to 3 ft.
